content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":3,"description_fidelity":5,"readability_1x":7,"pixel_craft":5,"palette_discipline":4,"appeal":5},"score":46,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["The rounded white dome and dangling legs read more like a simplified Mario Blooper than a mechanical Mega Man enemy.","The face uses three isolated black blocks with no clear red-flashing eye design or mine-like threat cue.","The lower tentacles are thin, uneven, and visually tangled at 1x; the center-right black pixels merge into an unclear mass.","The upper-right body edge loses a consistent dark outline, while the lower edge alternates abruptly between blue and black.","Black, white, light blue, and dark blue create four opaque colors, exceeding a normal NES sprite palette unless built from overlapping hardware sprites.","The body has little Capcom-style mechanical construction: no seam, casing division, rivet, intake, or weapon component."],"fixes":["Replace the three facial dots with a symmetrical two-eye unit, reserving one palette color for the normal/red-alert eye state.","Square off the dome slightly and add a 1-pixel casing seam or central metal plate to make it robotic rather than organic.","Redraw the bottom as two or three bold 2-pixel-wide tentacle clusters with clean negative-space gaps and distinct gathered/thrust animation poses.","Use a continuous dark contour around the upper shell and remove the ambiguous black clump at the lower right.","Reduce the sprite to black plus two body colors and transparency per hardware sprite, or deliberately separate the eye layer as an overlapping sprite palette.","Broaden the silhouette near the lower body and add one compact mine-like detail, such as a blinking core or armored side pods."]}
